content.user_title: Chart Complex Work with Issue Maps
content.value_statement: Large efforts can exceed one agent session and lose decisions across conversations. Wayfinder turns the work into an issue map with focused tickets, dependencies, and resolutions.
actual_capabilities: Creates a map issue with notes, decisions so far, and unresolved fog.
Breaks a large goal into child tickets for research, prototypes, grilling, or tasks.
Uses tracker-specific operations, with a local markdown tracker fallback when guidance is absent.
Claims one frontier ticket before work starts so concurrent sessions avoid duplicate work.
Records each resolution on its ticket and updates the map with a context pointer.
limitations: Requires an issue tracker or an agreed local markdown tracking process.
Does not resolve more than one ticket in a single session.
Depends on companion skills when grilling, domain modeling, or prototypes are needed.
Needs accurate dependency links or clear body conventions to identify blocked work.

use_cases.title: Plan a Multi-Session Engineering Effort
use_cases.description: Turn a broad migration, redesign, or refactor into linked issues with clear order and ownership.

use_cases.title: Organize Open Research
use_cases.description: Separate uncertain questions into focused tickets and preserve findings as linked resolution records.

use_cases.title: Shape Course or Product Work
use_cases.description: Convert a loose concept into decisions, task tickets, and fog that can become later work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a New Map
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: start from a loose idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Wayfinder to chart this idea into an issue tracker map: [describe the goal]. Ask only necessary clarifying questions, create the map, and create tickets that are clear now.

prompt_templates.title: Continue an Existing Map
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: work from a map URL or issue number.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Wayfinder with this map: [map link or issue number]. Load the map, choose the first unblocked and unclaimed frontier ticket, claim it, and resolve only that ticket.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a Named Ticket
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: focus on one known ticket.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Wayfinder to resolve this ticket from the map: [ticket title or link]. Claim it first, inspect only needed context, record the resolution, and update the map pointer.

prompt_templates.title: Replan After a Decision
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: update the map after new information changes the path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Wayfinder to process this new decision: [decision]. Update affected tickets, clear any fog that is now specific, create new tickets when needed, and preserve prior resolution links.

output_examples.input: A team wants to migrate authentication but does not know every decision yet.
output: A map issue records the goal, known constraints, and unresolved fog.
Child tickets cover provider research, session model decisions, migration risks, and rollout planning.
Blocking links show which questions must be answered before implementation work begins.

output_examples.input: A user provides an existing map and asks what to do next.
output: The agent loads the map at low resolution and finds the first open frontier ticket.
The ticket is claimed before work starts so parallel sessions do not duplicate effort.
The answer is posted as a resolution comment, and the map gets a concise decision pointer.

output_examples.input: A ticket answer reveals two new questions that were previously unclear.
output: The unclear fog is removed from the map once it becomes specific.
New child tickets are created for the two questions and linked to the correct dependencies.
The closed ticket remains the single detailed source for the decision that created them.

best_practices: Keep the map as an index and store detailed answers on the resolved ticket.
Claim a ticket before starting work so concurrent agents can avoid conflicts.
Resolve one ticket per session and create follow-up tickets only after the answer is known.
anti_patterns: Do not paste every open ticket body into the map.
Do not resolve tickets during the same session that creates the initial map.
Do not refer to tickets only by bare numbers when humans need readable names.

faq.question: What does Wayfinder create?
faq.answer: It creates a map issue and child tickets that organize a large goal into sequenced decisions and tasks.

faq.question: Can it work without a hosted issue tracker?
faq.answer: Yes, the skill says to use a local markdown tracker when tracker-specific documentation is absent.

faq.question: Why does it resolve only one ticket per session?
faq.answer: The limit keeps each session focused and preserves clear resolution records for later sessions.

faq.question: How does it handle parallel work?
faq.answer: Each session claims a ticket by assigning it before work begins, so other sessions can skip it.

faq.question: Does the map store every detail?
faq.answer: No. The map indexes decisions and links to tickets, while detailed answers stay on their own tickets.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
